```{r}

library(httr)
library(jsonlite)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)

api_key <- Sys.getenv("MY_API_KEY_ENV")

# api_key <- readLines("api-key")

# Set up the headers
my_headers <- add_headers(
  "x-access-token" = api_key,
  "Content-Type" = "application/json"
)

# Define the URL
url <- "https://api.openuv.io/api/v1/forecast?lat=52.98&lng=-1.16&alt=100&dt="

# Make the GET request
response <- GET(url, my_headers)

# Check the status code and content
if (status_code(response) == 200) {
  # Parse the JSON response
  result <- fromJSON(content(response, "text", encoding = "UTF-8"))
  #print(result)
} else {
  # Handle errors
  print(paste("Error:", status_code(response), content(response, "text")))
}

#print(str(response))

df <- result$result |>
    dplyr::mutate(uv_time = ymd_hms(uv_time))
 
library(scales) # Needed for better date/time formatting

df <- result$result |> dplyr::mutate(uv_time = ymd_hms(uv_time)) 

# Create the plot
df |> ggplot(aes(x = uv_time, y = uv, group = 1)) + 
  geom_point(color = "orange") + 
  geom_line(color = "darkgrey") +
  # Detailed X-axis configuration
  scale_x_datetime(
    date_breaks = "1 hour",          # Adds a label every hour
    date_labels = "%H:%M",           # Shows time as 13:00, 14:00, etc.
    minor_breaks = "30 mins"         # Adds small grid lines every 30 mins
  ) +
  labs(
    title = paste("Detailed UV Forecast for", format(Sys.Date(), "%d %B %Y")),
    x = "Time (24h Format)",
    y = "UV Index"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 0.5)) # Tilts text for better fit

```
